title: Regular expressions: `Pattern`, `Matcher` and the cost of backtracking

videos.script: A regular expression is a small program for reading text, written in a language of its own. {{match}} It can say whether a line is a log entry, and hand back the date, the title and the reader inside it by name. {{replace}} It can split a messy list, rewrite a date, and replace each number in a sentence by what a function makes of it, as a stream of matches. {{cost}} And it can take a very long time. Some patterns try every way of dividing the text before they give up, and each extra letter doubles the work. Twenty-eight letters took eleven seconds. {{guard}} Which is why a pattern typed by somebody else is never compiled as a pattern. It is quoted, and searched for as the text it is.
